name: Fused-Head Construction

dimensions.form: A non-nominal constituent realizes the NP without an overt nominal head
dimensions.meaning: Head interpretation is recovered from the constituent itself, context, or a licensed complement structure
dimensions.function: Head-like realization of an NP slot by a determiner, modifier, or related constituent
dimensions.distribution: NP positions where a nominal head is omitted, absent, or constructionally unrecovered

1.definition: A non-nominal constituent functions as the head of an NP without an overt nominal head
1.details: This family covers fused determiner-head uses and fused modifier-head uses. The overt constituent may be a DP, an adjective phrase, a participial phrase, or a related non-nominal expression, depending on the subtype. The point of the construction is that the NP's head interpretation is supplied without an overt noun.

constraints.description: The construction lacks an overt nominal head and is realized by a non-nominal constituent whose head interpretation is recoverable.
Fused determiner-head and fused modifier-head uses are subtypes of this broader family.

relatedConstructions.notes: The fused constituent realizes a complete NP without a separate nominal head.

grounds.note: CGEL's fused-head analysis covers determiner-head and modifier-head uses

projection.target: The contrast between some left and the poor left is not merely the same omitted noun. The rich can denote humans without a recoverable nominal, while an anaphoric adjective NP can take its interpretation and number from the previously named nominal.
projection.evidence: CGEL distinguishes fusion of determiner and modifier with head and separates simple, partitive, and special interpretations.

curious.title: Noun phrases with no noun
curious.summary: Some phrases work as a full noun phrase even though the main word isn't a noun.
curious.body:
A noun phrase is a phrase that can name people or things. In Everybody left early and The rich were taxed more heavily, the phrases work that way, yet neither has a noun in it. Rich is a describing word, and the phrase has no separate noun after it.

In each phrase, the job of the noun is done by another word. We still know what is meant, because the meaning is supplied by the word itself, by the context, or by what follows. This dictionary calls the pattern a fused head.
curious.try: In The rich were taxed more heavily, what noun could you add after rich? Does the sentence need it?

teacher.summary: For advanced classes: NPs whose head is a determinative or modifier with no overt noun.
teacher.explain: In a fused-head NP, a non-nominal constituent functions as the head without an overt nominal head, and the head interpretation is supplied without a noun. The family covers fused determiner-head uses (Everybody left early) and fused modifier-head uses (The rich were taxed more heavily). The overt constituent may be a determinative phrase (DP), an adjective phrase, a participial phrase or a related expression, depending on the subtype. The difference between some left and the poor left isn't just the same omitted noun: the rich can denote humans without a recoverable nominal, while an anaphoric adjective NP can take its interpretation and number from the nominal named earlier.
teacher.terms: Fused head is CGEL's analysis. Everybody is traditionally an indefinite pronoun, and the rich is sometimes described as an adjective used as a noun.

examples.text: She chose the red scarf and I chose [the blue].

contrasts.text: The rich were taxed more heavily.
contrasts.note: Human-class reading with no recoverable noun.

contrasts.text: She chose the red scarf and I chose the blue.
contrasts.note: The noun is recovered from the earlier scarf.

watch_for: A learner might think every fused head is just a noun that was deleted, when the rich needs no recoverable noun.
A learner might treat a determinative and an adjective as the same kind of fused head, when this dictionary separates fused determiner-head and fused modifier-head subtypes.
teacher.activity: Students sort sentences with no overt noun (Everybody left; the rich; I chose the blue) by where the meaning comes from: the word itself, context, or an earlier noun.

checked.note: Fixed: removed the claim that Everybody belongs with words like every and some (the entry only gives Everybody as a fused determiner-head example); in teacher text, the list of possible overt constituents now gives DP as determinative phrase, as in the entry.
